competitors.why: Azure and Azure AI compete with hyperscaler cloud providers for the same enterprise cloud and AI workloads (10-K Item 1: 'Our AI offerings compete with AI products from hyperscalers'); the 10-K names no company, so this is the engine's attribution of the hyperscaler class. Whole-company numbers only; AWS segment not retrieved.

competitors.name: Alphabet (Google Cloud, Workspace, Gemini, Search)
competitors.why: Google Cloud competes with Azure/Azure AI as a hyperscaler; Workspace with Microsoft 365; Search advertising with Bing (10-K Item 1 names hyperscalers and search engines without naming companies). Whole-company numbers only; Google Cloud segment not retrieved.

competitors.name: Oracle (OCI, database, Fusion and NetSuite applications)
competitors.why: OCI competes for AI infrastructure and database workloads; Oracle database competes with SQL Server/Azure data services and Fusion/NetSuite with Dynamics (10-K Item 1: database, BI, data warehousing and business-solution providers, unnamed). Whole-company numbers only.

bottlenecks.reading: Scarce input: datacenter power, land, permits and server capacity. MSFT states electricity generation, transmission and grid connection are capacity constrained in many regions, that its capacity build depends on land, zoning and permits, and that demand above available capacity limits its ability to serve customers. Others adding capacity are the other hyperscalers; how long the shortage lasts is not stated in the filing (gap).
Paid demand shown in MSFT own numbers: Azure revenue $33,165m vs $22,384m a year earlier (+48%), Microsoft Cloud $63.9bn (+30%), commercial remaining performance obligation $677bn (+73%).

The 10-Q warns demand for cloud and AI is hard to forecast and that overestimated demand or misaligned capacity may cause underutilization and asset impairment; operating costs and margins pressured by datacenter and device investment. Counter-risk to the shortage reading.
Hypothesis: AI strategy depends on third-party model partners, many of whom also compete with MSFT (10-Q risk factor); the OpenAI dependency is not sized in this lane.

notes: fd NAMED COMPETITORS (10-K Item 1): the 10-K names NO competitor companies, only classes: Office vs software and global application vendors, web/mobile and AI-first application companies; Windows vs alternative platforms and devices; Defender for Endpoint vs endpoint security providers; EMS vs identity and security vendors; LinkedIn vs online professional networks, job boards, recruiting and L&D providers; Dynamics vs cloud and on-premises business solution providers; Azure vs cloud service providers and open source, AI vs hyperscalers and other emerging competitors, many also partners; server products vs Unix/Linux vendors; Devices vs computer, tablet and hardware makers (many are partners); XBOX vs online gaming ecosystems and console platforms; Search vs search engines and web portals (pf_10k_20260729). The engine's attribution to AMZN, GOOGL, ORCL is its own, not the company's.

fd PEERS no prefetch/peers.json existed (prefetch had no --peers); competitor numbers are whole-company FY figures from each own SEC companyfacts (AMZN and GOOGL calendar 2025, ORCL fiscal year to May 2026), saved in gather/raw_field/. Periods differ from MSFT FY2026 (June). Competing-segment revenue (AWS, Google Cloud, OCI) NOT retrieved: not in companyfacts totals; gap.

fd MSFT SEGMENT Q1 FY2027 (Sep 2026) from release: Azure $33,165m vs $22,384m (+48%); Microsoft 365 cloud $27,778m vs $23,694m; Productivity and server licensing $8,407m vs $8,678m; Search and advertising $6,554m vs $5,942m; XBOX $5,379m vs $5,508m; Agents and Infra revenue $76.8bn +25%; Devices and Consumer $15.5bn -3%; Windows OEM and Devices -22% (pf_rel_20261028_1, release of 2026-10-28 is citable from 2026-10-30).

fd SHARE hypothesis: Azure at +48% grows faster than the consolidated revenue of AMZN (+12.4% FY2025), GOOGL (+15.1% FY2025) and ORCL (+17.4% FY2026), but those are whole-company figures, so no share conclusion about cloud can be drawn without AWS/Google Cloud/OCI segment revenue and without attributed share studies (not retrieved).

fd SHARE hypothesis: Search and advertising ex-TAC +12% against Alphabet whole-company growth of 15.1%: no search-share reading without Google Search segment numbers; labelled hypothesis, not evidence.
